title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: morte morieris — refuse spiritual death; Prima ratio; before GAR
pass_a_gloss: To this triple life you oppose a triple privation or death denounced by God to Adam as a penalty in the words you shall die the death, and you assert that man, just as God had threatened, was dead. But I (with your leave and that of others who think thus with you) cannot transfer those words you shall die the death to spiritual death or the privation of justice and sanctity. Hear, if you please, my reasons, and weigh them: for, unless my mind deceives me, they are not of nothing. First reason. A threat is opposed to a tacit promise, penalty to reward, the death denounced to the life promised. But the life tacitly promised to Adam was not justice or sanctity, unless you wish to confuse the condition of the promise with the thing promised. Therefore the death denounced was not the privation of justice.
pass_b_english: Against this threefold life you set a threefold privation or death, denounced by God to Adam as penalty in the words "you shall die the death," and you claim that man was dead just as God had threatened. For my part (with leave of you and of those who think with you) I cannot shift those words onto spiritual death—the loss of justice and sanctity. Hear my reasons, if you will, and weigh them; unless I am mistaken, they are not empty.

First reason. A threat answers a tacit promise, penalty answers reward, the death denounced answers the life promised. But the life tacitly promised to Adam was not justice or sanctity—unless you confuse the condition of the promise with the thing promised. Therefore the death denounced was not the privation of justice.
source_text: Huic triplici vitae triplicem opponis privationem seu mortem denunciatam a Deo Adamo ut poenam verbis, morte morieris, asserisque hominem, prout Deus minatus fuerat, mortuum esse. Ego vero (pace tua & aliorum, qui sic tecum sentiunt,) non possum verba illa morte morieris ad mortem spiritualem seu privationem justitiae & sanctitatis transferre. Audi, si placet, rationes meas, & expende: nam, nisi me fallit animus, non sunt de nihilo. Prima ratio. Comminatio opponitur tacite promissioni, poena praemio, mors denunciata vitae promissae. Atqui vita tacite promissa Adamo non erat justitia seu sanctitas, nisi velis promissionis conditionem cum re promissa confundere. Ergo mors denunciata non erat privatio justitiae.

choices.choice: Refuse spiritual-death transfer; threat answers promised life not condition
choices.why: Opens morte morieris case; stop before GAR
